summary:
Owner-words (safetynet-1) is close to its smaller spec: exact whole-message match, owner's own non-agent chat only, no action or tool, single notice, same restartBrain() and command for healing and /help, Docker StartedAt for the 10-minute floor, a stopped brain is never started, and /pause clears autoPaused with a truthful reply. I read the code and tests only; nothing was run.

Eight defects, none a lock-out:
- Two at severity 3. The restart holds no claim on Spark 2, so Stop, Start or Switch of the brain can race it. The page's Send lock is shared across chats, so with a hung brain the word cannot be typed in a new chat for up to five minutes without a reload.
- Four at severity 2. A '/' near miss with Sparkie down gets a generic error, not /help. /status reads healthy while a rerouted chat is dead. Four refusal guards have no test and one test comment claims a case it does not test. The by-hand resume line names the brain's Spark, not the console's.
- Two at severity 1. A wording slip ("1 minutes ago") and the missing R19 note.

Simplifications that keep the guard's intent: no claim-plus-rate-limit in favour of the shared flag and StartedAt floor (intent kept except for the claim, F1); the snapshot date dropped from /status along with /undo update; Telegram /status reusing statusText (masked, fixed template, no log or error text).
guardsKept: 1 Match only in the handler's chat branch, owner, non-agent chat, whole message, 40 chars max: kept (24-handler.mjs:628, 20-words.mjs:9-12). No URL or prefill sends a draft; the Cmd-K 'Ask Sparkie' auto-send is an explicit owner action and predates this.
2 Not an action; can only look, pause, or restart the existing container: kept. A stopped or missing container is refused, and there is no docker run or rm.
3 Restart only when running and started over 10 minutes ago by Docker's StartedAt: kept, with fail-closed on an unparseable time (wording defect F6).

4 Same restartBrain() with rendezvous removal, one in-flight flag that watchBrain checks, refused during brain start/stop/switch, audit line and fleet event: kept. 'Holds the claim on Spark 2 and releases it in a finally': missing, and not an acceptable simplification (F1).
5 Chat routed elsewhere: /restart says it would not help and changes nothing: kept. /status names the model but not that it is not answering: simplified, not ok (F4).
6 /status never waits on another Spark, 8 s cap, 'its server responds' wording, operations, pause state, internet state: kept. Snapshot date dropped along with /undo update: simplified, ok.

7 /pause sets halted true and autoPaused false, needs no passkey, truthful reply, both ways to resume, resuming never a word: kept. The by-hand line names the brain's Spark, not the console's (F7), and the auto-pause case is untested (F5).
8 Fixed templates, maskSecrets, stored as a notice, no model call: kept. The restart's error text goes only to the audit, masked, not into chat or the event.
9 Sparkie down and a '/' near miss gets /help: missing (F3). With Sparkie up it goes to Sparkie: kept.
10 No SSH, Tailscale, firewall, users, access, port, state file, secret or download: kept.
11 Architecture Today note under R11 and R19, plus the contract 8.13 note: R11 and 8.13 kept, R19 missing (F8).

12 Required tests: partly kept. Present: hung brain, near misses, member, agent conversation, ask_sparkie, loading and stopped refusals. Missing: refusal during a brain job, refusal while healing is mid-restart, stopped-brain /status, can-change key (F5).
13 Touch-only list: simplified, ok. 21-telegram.mjs also changed (tgStatusText now returns statusText()); 14-chats.mjs is untouched as required.
Extra, page: Send enabled for owner '/' drafts when Sparkie is down and the banner says 'Type /help': kept, but defeated in the hung-brain case by the tab-wide sending flag (F2).

findings.title: /restart sparkie holds no claim on Spark 2, so brain Stop/Start/Switch and deploys can race the restart
findings.where: service/src/20-heal.mjs:134-137 (restartBrain); service/src/20-words.mjs:48-61; service/src/24-handler.mjs:577-583, 586-593 (/main/use, /main/start, /main/stop check only mainBusy())
findings.fails: Sequence: the brain is hung, the owner types /restart sparkie (brainRestarting is true for up to 180 s), then presses Stop or Switch on Models. mainBusy() is false because the restart is not a job, and claimed([MAIN.node]) succeeds because nothing claimed Spark 2. `docker stop` then runs against an in-flight `docker restart`: the stop job reports success and the restart starts the container again, so the brain runs after a 'stopped' job. With Switch, the restart races the removal and run of the new container. In reverse, the word is not refused while a deploy or stop holds Spark 2 (busySparks), so the brain reloads tens of GB in the middle of that operation's memory measurement. Guard 4 asked for the claim held and released in a finally; only the in-flight flag was built. watchBrain has the same gap (R11/R19 'Today'), but the word makes it owner-triggered at exactly the moment the owner is also clicking around Models.
findings.fix: In restartBrain(), take `const release = claimSparks([MAIN.node], 'restarting Sparkie’s model')` before run() and release it in the finally. In restartWord and watchBrain, return early (busyWords / silently, before healMark) when `busySparks.has(MAIN.node)`, so the 409 is never thrown after the owner was told 'Restarting'.
findings.test: words.test.mjs: make the stand-in `docker restart` slow, say '/restart sparkie', then POST /main/stop and expect 409 'Something is already changing on Spark 2'. Also: while a deploy job holds spark2, '/restart sparkie' answers 'Nothing was changed' and no restart_sparkie audit line appears. Both pass wrongly today (202, and a restart).

findings.title: Page: Send is locked in every chat while one reply is stuck, so the word cannot be typed in the hung-brain case
findings.where: public/app.js:233 (state.chat.sending is one flag for all chats), :3725 (syncSend), :4028/:4065 (sendConsole), :4073 (send returns if c.sending)
findings.fails: Sequence: the brain is hung but /v1/models still returns 200 (the case /restart sparkie exists for). The owner sends a normal message; the stream stalls and c.sending stays true until the 300 s upstream timeout (service/src/14-chats.mjs:269). The owner clicks New and types /restart sparkie: Send is disabled and Enter is ignored, because c.sending is global to the tab. The server would answer (answerOwnerWord does not look at `replying`), but the page never sends it. The only way through is reloading the page, which nothing tells the owner.
findings.fix: Let an owner's '/' draft through while another chat's reply is pending: record which conversation is sending (c.sendingConv) and make syncSend/send block only when `c.sending && (c.sendingConv === c.conv?.id || !slashDraft())`. For that case post the word with its own small fetch, not the shared sendConsole state.
findings.test: Page check (browser or DOM test; I did not confirm a page test harness exists): with a stream held open in chat A, open New chat and type '/status'; Send must be enabled and the notice must appear. It is disabled today.

findings.title: Guard 9 missed: with Sparkie down, a '/' near miss gets a generic error, not the /help text
findings.where: service/src/24-handler.mjs:628-630; public/app.js:3724-3725 (Send enabled for any '/' draft when down)
findings.fails: Input: the brain is stopped and the owner types '/restart' or '/status please' (the page deliberately enables Send for any draft starting with '/'). ownerWord returns null, so the text goes to chatReply -> sparkieTurn, which saves it as a user turn and then fails on the model call (connection refused, or the 409 'No model…'). The owner sees an error toast or failed reply and no list of words. The spec says a non-exact '/' message with Sparkie down gets /help.
findings.fix: In the chat-message branch: `if (owner && !conv.agent && !word && text.trim().startsWith('/') && text.trim().length <= 40)`, look at the cached brain state (recentMain(), or chatTarget() not reachable) and, when it is not healthy, `return answerOwnerWord(res, conv, '/help', …)`. With Sparkie up, behaviour is unchanged.
findings.test: words.test.mjs: setBrain('exited'), wait past the 5 s cache, say '/restart'. Expect text starting '/help\nThese work even when Sparkie can’t answer' and no new model-requests line. Today this is an error.

findings.title: /status reads healthy while chat is dead when Sparkie's chat is routed to another model
findings.fails: Setup: ROUTES.chat is an endpoint on Spark 3 and the owner powers Spark 3 off. /status answers 'Sparkie: running, and its server responds.' followed by 'Sparkie’s chat runs on X right now, not on its own model.' It never says X is not answering; the owner has to infer that from the 'Sparks online' line. Guard 5 asked for 'which model and that it is not answering'. The /restart refusal for this case (line 45) is correct.
findings.fix: When chat.kind === 'endpoint', add a state from cached knowledge only (no wait): `knownOffline(nodeById(chat.node)) ? ' Its Spark is off, so chat can’t answer.' : ''`. Put that line first, before the 'Sparkie:' line, so the headline is not a healthy one.
findings.test: words.test.mjs: set the chat route to a running model on spark3, mark spark3 offline, say '/status' and expect /chat runs on .* Its Spark is off/. Then say '/restart sparkie' and expect 'wouldn’t help. Nothing was changed.' with no audit line. The endpoint branch has no test at all today.

findings.title: Tests pass with the restart guards removed; one test comment claims a case it does not test
findings.fails: The spec's required tests 'refused during a brain job' and 'refused while healing is mid-restart' are absent. Deleting both mainBusy() checks or both brainRestarting checks in 20-words.mjs:48-57 leaves every test green. Also untested: /pause while an automatic pause is on (autoPaused must become false and the reply must be 'Paused.', not 'Already paused.'), and ask_sparkie '/pause' from a can-change key (the test uses a look key). Lines 70-73: the comment says 'With Sparkie's model stopped, /status still answers', but setBrain('running') runs first and the assertion is /Sparkie: running/, so the stopped-brain /status is never exercised. That same assertion can read a 5-second-old 'exited' from recentMain's cache and flake.
findings.fix: Add four cases: (a) POST /main/stop, then '/restart sparkie' while the job runs -> 'being started, stopped or switched'; (b) slow stand-in restart, a second '/restart sparkie' -> 'already restarting', exactly one audit line; (c) set autoPaused:true, halted:true, then '/pause' -> 'Paused.' and autoPaused false; (d) '/status' while setBrain('exited') -> 'Sparkie: stopped.', before setting it back to running.
findings.test: These are the tests; (a) and (b) fail if the mainBusy or brainRestarting checks are removed, (c) fails if `autoPaused: false` is dropped from pauseWord.

findings.title: Loading refusal says '1 minutes ago', and claims a start time when Docker gave none
findings.fails: For upMs under 30 s, Math.max(1, round) prints 1 but the plural test uses the unclamped round (0), giving 'started 1 minutes ago'. If StartedAt is empty or unparseable, `Date.parse(...) || Date.now()` makes upMs 0, and the owner is told the model 'started 1 minutes ago and may still be loading', which is untrue. Refusing is the right fail-closed result; the words are wrong.
findings.fix: Compute `const mins = Math.max(1, Math.round(upMs / 60000))` once and use it for both the number and the plural. When StartedAt does not parse, answer 'Couldn’t tell when Sparkie’s model started. Nothing was changed.'
findings.test: words.test.mjs: write started-sparkie-main as now minus 10 s -> /started 1 minute ago/. Write 'garbage' -> /Couldn’t tell when/.

findings.title: By-hand resume line names the brain's Spark, not the console's, and disappears from /help when no brain is set up
findings.fails: The settings file lives in STATE_DIR on the console's host, but the reply says 'by hand on ${sparkName(mainNode())}', the brain's node. They are the same Spark today (spark2 in config.json). After a switch to a brain setup on another Spark, the owner is sent to a machine where the file does not exist, and this is the only passkey-free way to resume. Also helpWord prints both by-hand lines only `if (MAIN)`, so with no brain configured /help omits the resume line although /pause still works.
findings.fix: Name the console's own node (the node whose host is 'local', falling back to the configured hub) for the settings-file line in both places, and move the 'resume agents’ changes' line outside the `if (MAIN)`.
findings.test: words.test.mjs: with a brain setup whose node is spark3, '/pause' and '/help' still say 'by hand on Spark 2: set "halted": false'.

findings.title: R19 'Today' note not updated for the second caller of restartBrain
findings.fails: Guard 11 asked for the note under both R11 and R19. R19 still says only watchBrain's restart goes through run with no claim, and its bound 'two brain restarts in six hours' reads as covering all brain restarts. The owner's word is not counted against that bound and is limited only by the 10-minute StartedAt floor. A later builder reading R19 gets a wrong picture.
findings.fix: Add to R19's Today sentence: the owner's '/restart sparkie' (R34) calls the same restartBrain(), is not counted in the two-in-six-hours bound, and is limited by Docker's StartedAt (10 minutes). If F1 is fixed, change 'no claim' accordingly.
findings.test: Review only (documentation).

verdicts.why: Confirmed. restartBrain() (service/src/20-heal.mjs:134-137) only sets brainRestarting and calls run(); it never calls claimSparks. brainRestarting is read only in 20-heal.mjs and 20-words.mjs, so /main/stop, /main/start and /main/use (24-handler.mjs:577-593) check mainBusy() plus claimed([MAIN.node]) and both pass during a restart. stopMain's `docker stop --time 60` (13-main-model.mjs:272) can then run against an in-flight `docker restart --time 30`, and a deploy onto Spark 2 is not blocked either. In reverse, restartWord (20-words.mjs:48-57) never looks at busySparks, so the word restarts the brain while a deploy or stop holds Spark 2. Guard 4 says the word 'holds the claim on Spark 2 and releases it in a finally'; dropping the claim is not a simplification that keeps the guard's intent, because the in-flight flag only protects restart against restart. Severity 3 is fair (owner-triggered, at the moment the owner is also using Models; result is a 'stopped' job with the brain running, or a switch racing a restart).
verdicts.fix: In restartBrain(): after the brainRestarting check, `if (busySparks.has(MAIN.node)) return null;` then `const release = claimSparks([MAIN.node], 'restarting Sparkie’s model')` and call release() in the existing finally. In restartWord, add `|| busySparks.has(MAIN.node)` to both mainBusy() checks (20-words.mjs:48 and :56) so the refusal comes before 'Restarting' is said; in watchBrain add the same test to the line-145 condition, before healMark. Test (words.test.mjs): slow stand-in `docker restart`, say '/restart sparkie', POST /main/stop expects 409 'Something is already changing on Spark 2'; and with a deploy job holding spark2, '/restart sparkie' answers 'Nothing was changed' with no restart_sparkie audit line.

verdicts.why: Confirmed. state.chat.sending is one flag for the tab (public/app.js:233). sendConsole sets it at :4028 and clears it only in the finally at :4065, after streamChat returns; streamChat (:2470-2492) has no AbortController and no page-side timeout. syncSend (:3725) disables Send whenever c.sending, regardless of slashDraft(), and send() returns at :4073. The upstream model call has a 300 s idle timeout (service/src/14-chats.mjs:269, :304), so after one stalled message the owner cannot send /status or /restart sparkie from any chat in that tab for up to five minutes per model step. The server side would answer (the chat-message branch at 24-handler.mjs:628-629 runs before chatReply's `replying` check at 14-chats.mjs:182). This is exactly the 'running but stuck' case the word exists for; only a reload or a second tab gets through, and nothing says so. Severity 3.
verdicts.fix: Smallest: in syncSend use `sendBtn.disabled = (c.sending && !slashDraft()) || (!sparkieModel().up && !slashDraft())`, and in send(), when c.sending and the text is one of the four words (same trim/lowercase/underscore rule), post it with its own streamChat call to the current chat (or a new one) and append the returned notice, without touching c.sending or the streaming reply. Test: page/DOM check with a stream held open in chat A; type '/status' and expect Send enabled and the notice shown. No page test harness was found in test/, so this may need a manual check listed in the change.

verdicts.why: Confirmed missed guard. Guard 9: 'With Sparkie down, an owner message starting with / that is not an exact word gets the /help text'. 24-handler.mjs:628-630 only handles an exact ownerWord; anything else goes to chatReply. The page deliberately enables Send for any '/' draft when Sparkie is down (app.js:3724-3725), so '/restart' or '/status please' is saved as a user turn and fails on the model call with an error toast. Nothing in app.js maps near misses to /help client-side (only the banner text at :3810 'Type /help for what still works', which softens it). Severity 2: nothing is changed wrongly, but the owner in an outage gets an error instead of the list.
verdicts.fix: In the chat-message branch after the word check: if `owner && !conv.agent && text.trim().startsWith('/') && text.trim().length <= 40`, read the brain state without waiting long (recentMain() raced against a short sleep, or chatTarget() missing) and when it is not running and healthy, `return await answerOwnerWord(res, conv, '/help', via)`. With Sparkie up, unchanged. Test (words.test.mjs): setBrain('exited'), wait past the 5 s cache, say '/restart'; expect text starting '/help\nThese work even when Sparkie can’t answer' and no new model-requests line.

A live probe of the other Spark would break guard 6 (never wait on another Spark), so the cached form is the right size. The /restart refusal at :45 is correct. The endpoint branch has no test. ' Its Spark isn’t reachable, so chat can’t answer.' : ''}`, and put that line before the 'Sparkie:' line. Test: route chat to a running model on spark3, mark spark3 offline, '/status' matches /chat runs on .* Its Spark isn’t reachable/; then '/restart sparkie' answers 'wouldn’t help. No test starts a main-start/stop/switch job before the word, and none sends a second word while a restart is in flight, so removing the mainBusy() or brainRestarting checks at 20-words.mjs:48-49 and :56-57 leaves all six tests green; guard 12 lists both as required. /pause is only tested from the un-paused state (:79) and from an owner pause (:85), so dropping `autoPaused: false` at :36 still passes (:83 only asserts not-true from a state where it was never true). ask_sparkie uses a look key (:13, :104), not a can-change key as the guard says. summary:
Read-only review of dark-readings (power-2). The build matches the smaller version closely: sysfs-only readings printed before the docker look, numbers or null, no new event type, no health argument, verdicts or limits table, no tuning advice, worker.py and workflow code lists untouched (none of the edited functions are in any `code()` list in service/src/18-workflows.mjs:25-53). The readings script is safe under `bash -s` with files missing, and the restart test (`upSeconds*1000 <= darkMs + 60000`) holds because detection lag is at most about 36 s (ConnectTimeout=6, 30 s status).

I found four real defects, none of which can lock the owner out or change anything on a Spark; all are about truthfulness to the owner.

1. A console restart while a Spark is dark writes a second spark-offline with no reading, and both `darkPeriods` and fleet_status pick that later one. The real time and the last reading are lost, in exactly the "went dark overnight, asked in the morning after an install" case.
2. A last reading with no GPU numbers (nvidia-smi failed, which worker.py reports as null) is called "idle ... not counted as a fault".
3. fleet_status gives an offline Spark `lastReadingBeforeDark.ageSeconds` with no time it went dark, so "20 seconds" reads as now. It can also show a reading from an older, finished dark period.
4. Two guards have no test: the 90-second floor and the three-minute freshness cut. The suite passes with either line deleted.

I ran nothing; the findings are from reading the code and the stand-ins.
guardsKept: 1. Readings first, script ends exit 0, parsed before exit-code check: kept, simplified ok. No literal `exit 0` was added, but the readings never change how the script ends (it ends on the docker pipeline as before), and `watchSpark` parses `read` before `r.code !== 0` (19-watcher.mjs:126-128). The missing-files test exists (dark.test.mjs:57-63).
2. Every reading a range-checked number or null, no device text: kept. `reading()` at 19-watcher.mjs:53; the zone is digit-checked in the shell, NVMe and fan in JS.

3. spark-offline carries a reading only when under three minutes old: kept in code (`lastReading`, FRESH_READING_MS), untested (dark-4). 'No reading near the time' is said only in the restarted finding; the event and fleet_status just carry null. Defeated in practice by the duplicate offline event after a console restart (dark-1).

4. No finding from a temperature limit; shows number, age and gap to nvidia-smi: kept, simplified ok. Findings key on restart and GPU busy or watts only; gpuC and hottestC are shown side by side rather than as a computed gap. Online Sparks in fleet_status show hottestC without its age (up to 3 minutes old), which is minor. 'Never rule heat out' is kept, except the no-GPU-numbers case is called idle (dark-2).
5. 'Did not restart' wording: kept (19-watcher.mjs:79).
6. Restart from idle = consistent with switched off by hand, not a fault: kept (19-watcher.mjs:82). Marking console-made shutdowns: not applicable yet, since the console has no power-off action.
7. Real window, at most five: kept (`since: events[0]?.at`, `slice(0, max)`).

8. fleet_status with {} runs no command, no new argument, no new tool; description says which temperature is which; one code-built sentence per Spark: partly kept. Schema unchanged and description is clear. The per-Spark sentence is missing from fleet_status (`readingWords` is used only in `describeEvent`); not ok for the offline entry, where the bare ageSeconds misleads (dark-3).
9. No new event type, no extra events, under 90 s ignored as in cameBack: kept in code (same HEAL_OFFLINE_MS), untested (dark-4).

10. worker.py unchanged, no workflow code() function edited: kept as far as readable. None of the touched functions appear in 18-workflows.mjs:25-53; only test/mock/worker.py gained status.json. I could not byte-compare service/worker.py (no git here).
11-15. Probe, kernel log, shutdown records, busctl guards: not built, as the smaller version says. Nothing to check.
16. No tuning command in any advice line: kept. No advice text was added.
17. Hostile-text acceptance test restated: not applicable. No outside text is added by this item; fleet_status stays in INSIDE_READS with numbers only.

findings.title: Console restart while a Spark is dark replaces the real dark time and its last reading with an empty one
findings.fails: `knowledge.sparks[id].online` is saved only when the watcher sees a container change (19-watcher.mjs:232), so knowledge.json usually still says online:true after a Spark goes dark. Sequence: Spark 4 goes dark at 02:13 under load (spark-offline written with `last`). The console restarts at 08:00 (an install, a crash, a reboot of Spark 2). The first status round sees stale online:true against unreachable and writes a second spark-offline with `last: null`, because the stored gpu and readings are over three minutes old. Spark 4 returns at 08:41. `darkPeriods` keeps the later offline event, so spark_diagnostics says it went dark at 08:00, dark 41 minutes, 'restarted; there was no reading near the time it went dark'. While it is still dark, fleet_status `events.findLast(...)?.last` gives `lastReadingBeforeDark: null`. The evidence the feature exists for is on disk and is hidden.
findings.fix: In `darkPeriods` keep the first offline of a run: `if (e.type === 'spark-offline') off ||= e;`. verdicts.why: Confirmed. knowledge.json is written in one place only (service/src/19-watcher.mjs:232, `if (changed || learned) saveKnowledge()`), and a Spark that stops answering makes watchSpark return false at :127 before it marks anything changed, so the file normally keeps `online: true` for a dark Spark. summary:
Read-only review of the paste card (everywhere-1) and the brain cap (R36). Nothing was run, so every finding is from reading the source. The core is sound: the card is built by code, the model never sees the block, it is appended once from the action's value, and the count has no race and frees on every ending I could trace. There is no lock-out path and nothing changes on a Spark.

The "one generic card, no clients.json" simplification keeps the intent of the row-checking, basis-line and capability-line guards, because the text is now constants that only change by install.

Six defects, none above severity 3:
- **Context figure (3):** the card hands apps 1,000,000 tokens with no 262,144 ceiling, which is the slot-holding risk the attack named.
- **Non-brain target (3):** when `sparkie` points at another model the card still gives a full block, with no "tool calls are not known".
- **Untested "minus one" (3):** the stand-in brain answers 1 at once, so the reservation branch and the "no cap when unset" branch never run in a test.
- **Result shape (2):** with `client` the action returns the whole `running_models` result with `paste` last; on a busy fleet the 12,000-character cut can drop the "it is shown" notice, and the model can still write its own block from `gateway.baseUrl`.
- **429 wording (2):** "one place stays for the owner's chat" is untrue when the brain answers 1 at once, and agent-door and Telegram turns are not counted either.
- **Claude match (1):** any app name containing "claude" is answered as "Claude Code".
